checks.mutation_check: Ran every proposed test against the OLD substring implementation before trusting them. THREE were vacuous (passed on the broken code, proving nothing) and their comments overclaimed: a password or db-name containing 'localhost' CANNOT trigger the old over-match, because '@' must be percent-encoded in userinfo. That is now test_remote_host_merely_starting_with_localhost_requires_ssl, and it fails against the old implementation. Exactly 2 of 8 tests are true regressions; the file labels which are REGRESSION and which are guards.

checks.independent_review: DONE - security-focused, adversarial. Verdict: cannot disable TLS on prod RDS. Reviewer traced infrastructure/ecs.tf:571 (DB_HOST = aws_db_instance.main.address = the RDS FQDN) and service_discovery.tf (registers only `whisper`, so no postgres/db VPC alias exists), and produced an old-vs-new divergence table: the ONLY shape where new is weaker than old is a bare host of exactly `postgres`, which Terraform makes unreachable. Confirmed '::1' is not dead code (make_url strips brackets -> .host == '::1'), case is preserved (no path folds a remote host into a local name), and the 'exactly 2 of 8 tests are true regressions' claim. Three findings fixed here: (1) make_url raises a BARE ValueError on a bad/empty port, which `except ArgumentError` let escape at import — my docstring's 'fails closed on an unparseable URL' was therefore FALSE; now `except (ArgumentError, ValueError)` + 2 tests. (2) '::1' and the hostless-socket path had zero coverage -> tests added. (3) The prod composition (_resolve_database_url JSON envelope -> _ssl_connect_args) was untested -> TestResolvedProdUrlRequiresSsl added. Also corrected alerts.md, which described the latent over-match as though PHI had actually been sent in plaintext; it was never reachable. Deferred (pre-existing, not this diff): _resolve_database_url interpolates the password unquoted, so a password containing '@' would hijack the parsed host — unreachable (AWS RDS master-password constraints exclude @ / " and space) and it would fail at NXDOMAIN before reaching RDS; fix is urllib.parse.quote(password, safe='').
